feedback: The device remains personally owned under the statute.
Correct. The rules expressly allow those additions.
Additional requirements do not remove the baseline.
Recording remains required.

cards.title: Qualifying state connection
cards.front: What connections can support application?
cards.rule: Wyoming residence, a place of employment or practice, or the specified military spouse/dependent connection.
cards.boundary: Other eligibility conditions apply together.
cards.mixup: A Wyoming customer alone is not the listed connection.

cards.title: Lawful presence
cards.front: Which status alternatives appear?
cards.rule: Citizenship, permanent legal residency or otherwise lawful U.S. presence.
cards.boundary: The applicant must still meet age and other qualifications.
cards.mixup: Do not import a citizenship-only condition.

cards.title: Each-term learning
cards.front: When are education and exam repeated?
cards.rule: Both new and renewed commissions require the applicable education and examination.
cards.boundary: The state rule calls for every-term review and certification under its route.
cards.mixup: Experience does not create a lifetime learning exemption.

cards.title: Approved alternative
cards.front: How can approved provider completion be used?
cards.rule: Attach the approved education/exam certificate and skip Part III as instructed.
cards.boundary: The remainder of the application, including oath, still applies.
cards.mixup: An arbitrary purchased course is not an approved alternative.

cards.title: Current paper assessment
cards.front: What does the state form require for passing?
cards.rule: At least fourteen correct answers on its twenty true-or-false items.
cards.boundary: No numeric timer is established by the opened form.
cards.mixup: The remote signer's identity quiz is a different process.

cards.title: Application oath
cards.front: How is Part IV executed?
cards.rule: Swear or affirm and sign before another commissioned notary.
cards.boundary: The form expressly excludes doing it yourself.
cards.mixup: A supplier receipt does not replace the oath.

cards.title: Single authority
cards.front: How many Wyoming commissions can operate together?
cards.rule: Only one active Wyoming notary commission at a time.
cards.boundary: An official name update does not create a second commission.
cards.mixup: More employers do not multiply commissions.

cards.title: Six-year term
cards.front: How long does the new or renewed term run?
cards.rule: Six years under the statute.
cards.boundary: The name-change form preserves the existing term dates.
cards.mixup: An updated identity certificate is not automatically a renewal.

cards.title: Changed information
cards.front: How is the official record updated?
cards.rule: Notify the Secretary within thirty days through the prescribed form.
cards.boundary: Name changes also include the signature sample and fee.
cards.mixup: A business-card update does not change the state file.

cards.title: Criminal event notice
cards.front: What plea can trigger reporting?
cards.rule: A conviction or guilty/no-contest plea to the specified felony or fraud/dishonesty/deceit crime requires written notice within thirty days.
cards.boundary: The duty is separate from possible discipline.
cards.mixup: No-contest wording does not eliminate the report.

cards.title: Personal knowledge
cards.front: What identity assurance is required?
cards.rule: Interactions or corroboration dispel reasonable uncertainty about the claimed identity.
cards.boundary: A separate qualifying credential or witness route may be used.
cards.mixup: A familiar face alone may leave uncertainty.

cards.title: Credential recency
cards.front: Which expiration window applies?
cards.rule: The credential is current or expired no more than three years before the act.
cards.boundary: The officer must find it satisfactory and the rule requires a photograph.
cards.mixup: Do not treat all old IDs as acceptable indefinitely.

cards.title: Credible witness
cards.front: What makes a credible witness usable?
cards.rule: An honest, reliable, impartial person personally knows the principal and gives the identity oath or affirmation.
cards.boundary: The witness must be known or identified through the specified route.
cards.mixup: A stranger's confidence is not personal knowledge of the principal.

cards.title: Representative authority
cards.front: What is checked beyond identity?
cards.rule: The officer determines the claimed title or capacity using the record, personal knowledge or an official record.
cards.boundary: Execution must still be knowing and willing for the intended purpose.
cards.mixup: Identifying the person alone does not prove agency.

cards.title: Jurat commitment
cards.front: What does verification add?
cards.rule: The principal declares the statement true on oath or affirmation and signs knowingly and willingly before the officer.
cards.boundary: An affirmation is legally equivalent to an oath.
cards.mixup: The notary does not swear the principal's facts for them.

cards.title: Directed witness signature
cards.front: How can an unaffected witness sign for a physically unable principal?
cards.rule: Use the principal's direction in the officer's presence and the required notation.
cards.boundary: The witness must be unaffected by the record and identified.
cards.mixup: An interested helper does not satisfy the stated witness condition.

cards.title: Directed officer signature
cards.front: When can the officer sign for that principal?
cards.rule: The principal directs it in the presence of two unaffected witnesses, with the stated identifying notation.
cards.boundary: All participants appear in the required journal record.
cards.mixup: One witness is not enough for the officer-signing route.

cards.title: Official-copy exception
cards.front: Which official record exception is stated?
cards.rule: The officer may fit the prohibition's exception when employed by the entity issuing or holding the original.
cards.boundary: The copy still must be full, true and accurate.
cards.mixup: An unrelated private request does not create that employment exception.

cards.title: Interest prohibition
cards.front: Whose interests are included?
cards.rule: The officer's, spouse's and civil partner's stated party or direct beneficial interests.
cards.boundary: The chapter also addresses individual naming and self-signatures.
cards.mixup: A fee waiver does not remove an actual interest.

cards.title: Original-record access
cards.front: May an original be kept as leverage?
cards.rule: Do not withhold access or possession except as otherwise permitted by law.
cards.boundary: Receiving a record does not make it the officer's property.
cards.mixup: A commission itself does not grant a general lien.

cards.title: Mandatory journal
cards.front: What acts are chronicled?
cards.rule: All notarial acts go in one or more journals.
cards.boundary: The education presentation also addresses refusals and corrections.
cards.mixup: Unpaid acts do not fall outside the general journal duty.

cards.title: Flexible medium
cards.front: Must journal format match record format?
cards.rule: A tangible or electronic journal can chronicle acts on either record medium.
cards.boundary: Secure control applies regardless of format.
cards.mixup: A paper appointment does not categorically bar an electronic journal.

cards.title: Personal custody
cards.front: Who controls the journal?
cards.rule: The notary keeps it and other records secure under sole control.
cards.boundary: Surrender or destruction needs the specified authority.
cards.mixup: A shared unlocked drawer does not establish control.

cards.title: Employer copies
cards.front: What may an employer retain after departure?
cards.rule: A copy concerning employment-scope acts.
cards.boundary: Original surrender requires state approval and another officer cannot use the journal.
cards.mixup: Paying for the book does not authorize unrestricted original use.

cards.title: Journal loss
cards.front: How is journal loss reported?
cards.rule: Promptly notify the Secretary using the prescribed email or letter route.
cards.boundary: The rule provides a letter alternative without email access.
cards.mixup: A supplier replacement order does not notify the state.

cards.title: Stamp contents
cards.front: Which identity details are built into the stamp?
cards.rule: Commissioned name, Notary Public, State of Wyoming, identification number and expiration wording/date.
cards.boundary: The bordered rectangle and blue-or-black format also apply.
cards.mixup: Residence county and Great Seal imagery are excluded.

cards.title: Renewed stamp
cards.front: What happens at every renewed term?
cards.rule: Obtain a new compliant physical or electronic stamp.
cards.boundary: Handwritten additions cannot amend the required stamp content.
cards.mixup: An unchanged name does not waive replacement.

cards.title: Correction support
cards.front: What supports a later certificate text correction?
cards.rule: The transaction's journal evidence where applicable supports the change.
cards.boundary: Date and initial the correction and note it in the journal.
cards.mixup: A recipient's preferred outcome is not factual evidence.

cards.title: Authorized third-party edit
cards.front: What allows a third party to correct a certificate?
cards.rule: Only the original officer can authorize it, in writing, with the specified retained copies.
cards.boundary: The changed certificate and authorization accompany the journal record where applicable.
cards.mixup: Ownership of the paper does not grant unilateral correction authority.

cards.title: Disable old device
cards.front: What follows expiration, resignation or revocation?
cards.rule: Render the stamping device unusable by an authorized disabling means.
cards.boundary: Death or incompetency has duties for the listed possessor.
cards.mixup: A ready-to-use stamp is not transferred with the next job.

cards.title: Optional basic charge
cards.front: Must the maximum always be collected?
cards.rule: The officer can charge less or waive it.
cards.boundary: The basic fee ceiling still controls when charging.
cards.mixup: Free service does not waive ceremony or records.

cards.title: Basic ceiling
cards.front: What is the ordinary maximum?
cards.rule: Ten dollars per act, with the listed multi-person-on-one-record provision.
cards.boundary: Separate travel and technology fees have conditions.
cards.mixup: The filing fee is a different fee category.

cards.title: Technology agreement
cards.front: When is the technology total agreed?
cards.rule: Before the notarial act.
cards.boundary: Explain its separate and nonmandated character.
cards.mixup: A surprise after completion misses advance agreement.

cards.title: Travel timing
cards.front: When is travel fee agreement reached?
cards.rule: Before travel begins.
cards.boundary: The charge stays within the standard IRS mileage rate.
cards.mixup: Agreement only after arrival misses the travel condition.

cards.title: Separate explanation
cards.front: How are travel and technology charges described?
cards.rule: They are separate from the basic fee and neither specified nor mandated by law.
cards.boundary: Both have their own statutory conditions.
cards.mixup: Do not call a privately agreed surcharge a mandatory state tax.

cards.title: Advance payment
cards.front: Can compliant fees be collected first?
cards.rule: The officer may require advance payment.
cards.boundary: Refund treatment depends on the stated facts.
cards.mixup: Prepayment does not require the officer to complete an unlawful act.

cards.title: Failed proofing
cards.front: What discretion covers a compliant prepaid technology fee?
cards.rule: The fee may remain nonrefundable after required proofing fails for fraud or innocent reasons.
cards.boundary: The identity outcome still must be reported truthfully.
cards.mixup: A failed quiz does not itself prove fraud.

cards.title: Principal cancellation
cards.front: What short-notice travel case is listed?
cards.rule: The rule permits retaining a compliant prepaid travel fee when the principal cancels with less than twenty-four hours' notice.
cards.boundary: Other lawful-refusal grounds are separately listed.
cards.mixup: The exception does not authorize unlimited new penalty charges.

cards.title: Officer cancellation
cards.front: What refund rule covers officer cancellation without completion?
cards.rule: Refund the travel fee.
cards.boundary: This is different from the listed principal-cancellation permission.
cards.mixup: Prepayment alone does not override this rule.

cards.title: Employment policy
cards.front: Can an employer prohibit employee charges?
cards.rule: Yes, for acts performed as part of employment.
cards.boundary: The act and record requirements remain applicable.
cards.mixup: A no-fee policy does not transfer stamp ownership.

cards.title: Prior technology notice
cards.front: When is state notice made?
cards.rule: Before the first electronic-record or remotely located-person act, identify the intended technology.
cards.boundary: Same-room electronic format independently triggers notice.
cards.mixup: Only a webcam purchase does not provide state notice.

cards.title: RIN boundary
cards.front: What act does remote ink cover?
cards.rule: An acknowledgment on a tangible record.
cards.boundary: The principal first signs, dates and sends the ink record before the remote procedure.
cards.mixup: RIN is not a remote jurat method for every paper record.

cards.title: RON execution
cards.front: How is RON performed?
cards.rule: Use the compliant remote electronic-record procedure in one recorded session.
cards.boundary: The officer must be satisfied with record identity and technology quality.
cards.mixup: Perfect audio at one moment does not prove the whole act was completed properly.

cards.title: Entire communication
cards.front: What is recorded?
cards.rule: The entire remote communication audiovisually.
cards.boundary: Recording custody and official access have their own limits.
cards.mixup: A final seal screenshot is not the entire communication.

cards.title: Same record
cards.front: Who must be viewing the same record?
cards.rule: The principal and required witnesses, with reasonable confirmation steps by the officer.
cards.boundary: Both RIN and RON carry this duty.
cards.mixup: Matching filenames do not establish matching contents.

cards.title: Technology name
cards.front: What extra fact belongs in every remote certificate?
cards.rule: The actual electronic system or other communication technology name.
cards.boundary: The certificate also indicates remote method under the statute.
cards.mixup: A generic camera symbol does not name the system.

cards.title: Applicable proofing
cards.front: Can a remote system impose additional identity methods?
cards.rule: The statutory definition recognizes two or more different methods when required by the system or rule.
cards.boundary: Personal knowledge, credentials and credible-witness routes remain subject to applicable conditions.
cards.mixup: Do not invent a universal numerical KBA format from another state.

cards.title: Foreign principal
cards.front: What additional conditions apply outside the United States?
cards.rule: No foreign prohibition and a listed U.S. matter, property or transaction connection.
cards.boundary: The two conditions apply together.
cards.mixup: A U.S. record connection alone does not erase a local prohibition.

cards.title: Technology refusal
cards.front: When is refusal mandatory?
cards.rule: Refuse a request requiring a system that fails the act's standards.
cards.boundary: Unfamiliar or unsatisfactory technology also supports the stated discretionary refusal.
cards.mixup: A fee or waiver cannot make a noncompliant system lawful.

cards.title: Border authority
cards.front: What is checked before an allowable neighboring-state act?
cards.rule: The bordering state must recognize Wyoming authority and the officer follows Wyoming law and rules.
cards.boundary: Venue reflects actual physical location.
cards.mixup: Do not assume every bordering state recognizes authority without checking.

commission.summary: Wyoming terms last six years and require education and examination for each new or renewed commission.

sections.heading: Complete the application
sections.body: Meet age eighteen, the lawful U.S. status and the Wyoming residence, employment, practice or specified military-family connection. Complete the application and oath and certify education and examination. The January 2026 form directs hard-copy delivery or mail with check or money order. An approved-provider completion certificate permits skipping Part III, while the remaining required parts still apply.

sections.heading: Maintain the authority
sections.body: After processing, the state sends the appointment letter and certificate. Obtain the new compliant stamp using its details. Only one Wyoming commission can be active at once. Report changed information within thirty days. A name change includes the official-signature sample and separate fee, and the current form preserves the original term dates. Commissioning provides no public-official immunity.

example.heading: A provider-certificate renewal
example.body: A Casper notary completes an approved alternative course and exam. The certificate permits skipping the state form exam but does not remove Part IV. The applicant executes the oath before another commissioned notary and submits the remaining materials, then obtains the new-term stamp.

keyFacts: First and renewed terms require education and examination.
The state paper exam has twenty statements with fourteen correct required.
The term is six years.
A name change does not begin a fresh term.

acts.summary: Wyoming acts require satisfactory identity, knowing willing execution and a complete certificate for the actual procedure.

sections.heading: Establish the person and act
sections.body: Personal knowledge dispels reasonable uncertainty through interactions or corroboration. A qualifying government credential can be current or expired no more than three years, with the rule-required photograph. A credible witness personally knows the principal and gives the identity oath while being known or properly identified. Acknowledgment, witnessing and jurat have different execution conditions.

sections.heading: Apply special role conditions
sections.body: Representative capacity is established through the record, personal knowledge or an official record. Physical inability permits a directed unaffected-witness signature, or an officer signature with two unaffected witnesses, with the required notation and entries. Copy certification requires full, true and accurate reproduction. Official public-entity records have the stated issuing-or-holding-entity employment exception to the prohibition.

example.heading: Different source records
example.body: An independent Cheyenne notary receives a court-record copy request and a private copy request. The first triggers the official-record restriction unless the actual employment exception applies. The second still requires an accurate reproduction. Customer purpose and payment do not resolve either source status or accuracy.

keyFacts: Credentials meet recency and photograph requirements.
A jurat includes the principal's truth pledge.
Officer-directed signing requires two unaffected witnesses.
Spouse and civil-partner interests are separately screened.

records.summary: Wyoming journals chronicle all acts, and secure personal control applies to records and devices.

sections.heading: Protect the journal
sections.body: Maintain one or more tangible or electronic journals for acts on either record medium. The education presentation includes refusals and corrections. Keep records securely under sole control and do not permit another officer to use the journal. Original surrender at employment termination requires state approval, while the employer may retain the specified employment-scope copy. Promptly report journal or device loss through the prescribed route.

sections.heading: Correct the evidence properly
sections.body: The stamp uses the prescribed bordered rectangle, blue-or-black color and commission details, excluding the residence county and Great Seal. Each renewal requires a new physical or electronic stamp. Certificate text corrections need supporting transaction evidence where applicable, dated and initialed edits and a corresponding journal notation. Only the original officer makes or authorizes changes, with written third-party authorization and retained copies when that route is used.

example.heading: Text omission and stamp error
example.body: A Laramie notary finds an omitted certificate fact supported by the journal and a wrong stamp number. The text follows the correction process. The stamp image is not edited by hand. The officer obtains a corrected stamp and follows the permitted subsequent-impression procedure with the proper record.

keyFacts: All acts are chronicled regardless of payment.
Either journal medium can serve either record type.
Renewal requires a new stamp.
The performing officer controls certificate corrections.

fees.summary: Basic notarial fees, technology charges and travel fees have separate conditions and timing.

sections.heading: Agree to compliant charges
sections.body: The general notarial ceiling is ten dollars, with the listed multiple-person provision. Fees may be reduced or waived. Technology totals are agreed before the act with the separate nonmandated-charge explanation. Travel is agreed before the trip, stays within the standard IRS mileage rate and has its own separate-charge explanation. The chapter permits advance collection.

sections.heading: Use the actual refund facts
sections.body: Completed acts have the stated nonrefund discretion. A compliant prepaid technology fee may remain nonrefundable after required proofing fails for fraud or innocent reasons. The travel rule permits retaining prepaid travel for listed lawful refusal or principal cancellation with less than twenty-four hours notice. Officer cancellation without completion requires refund. An employer may prohibit charges for employment acts.

example.heading: Different cancellations
example.body: One principal cancels shortly before a mobile appointment. The notary cancels a separate appointment without completion. The rule permits retaining the compliant travel fee in the specified short-notice principal case and requires refund in the officer-cancellation case. The actual cancellation facts control.

keyFacts: The basic fee may be waived.
Technology agreement precedes the act.
Travel agreement precedes travel.
Officer cancellation without completion requires travel refund.

remote.summary: Wyoming separates remote online electronic acts from remote ink acknowledgment of tangible records.

sections.heading: Choose the lawful route
sections.body: Before the first electronic-record or remotely located-person act, notify the Secretary and identify intended technology. RON can cover authorized acts when the statutory conditions are met in one recorded session. RIN is limited to acknowledgment after the principal signs, dates and submits the tangible ink record. Both require reasonable steps ensuring the principal and required witnesses view the same record.

sections.heading: Preserve remote evidence
sections.body: Record the entire communication audiovisually and apply the statutory custody and official-access rules. The certificate indicates remote method and names the actual system under the rule. Applicable system or rule conditions may add identity methods. Overseas principals need both the no-prohibition and U.S.-nexus conditions. Bordering-state officer authority depends on recognition and Wyoming rules, with accurate actual venue.

example.heading: An ink jurat request
example.body: A principal mails an affidavit and asks for a remote ink jurat. RIN is defined as acknowledgment and cannot be used indiscriminately for every paper act. The notary explains that boundary and obtains lawful instructions for the actual requested act without certifying an unperformed oath.

keyFacts: Electronic format or remote location triggers prior notice.
RIN is a tangible acknowledgment.
The entire remote communication is recorded.
Remote certificates name the technology used.

articles.keyword: Wyoming remote ink begins with a signed tangible record
articles.title: Wyoming remote ink begins with a signed tangible record
articles.description: Follow RIN from the paper signature to the recorded acknowledgment.
articles.h1: Wyoming remote ink begins with a signed tangible record
articles.lede: Wyoming defines remote ink narrowly and gives it a specific order of events.

sections.heading: Identify the requested act
sections.body: A Jackson customer needs a paper agreement acknowledged while away from the notary. Wyoming's remote ink definition concerns an acknowledgment of a tangible record. This makes the requested act important before the parties choose a video method. A jurat or other sworn act cannot simply be relabeled RIN because the customer prefers paper and an ink signature.

sections.heading: Receive the signed paper
sections.body: The principal signs and dates the tangible record and submits the ink-signed document to the officer. The officer then initiates the remote act and establishes satisfactory identity of the principal or witness. This sequence distinguishes the ink execution from the later acknowledgment. The record already bears a signature, but the acknowledgment has yet to occur.

sections.heading: Complete the recorded procedure
sections.body: During the lawful remote communication, the principal acknowledges knowing and willing execution for the intended purpose. The officer takes reasonable steps to ensure the relevant participants view the same record. The entire communication is audiovisually recorded under the statute. Personal knowledge of the principal does not eliminate that separate recording requirement.

sections.heading: Describe the actual event
sections.body: The certificate describes acknowledgment on the actual notarial date and identifies the remote method and technology name. The journal chronicles the act, and the recording is secured under the statute's control rules. Signing the paper earlier does not justify dating the acknowledgment as if it occurred then or claiming that a different sworn-signature procedure was completed.

faqs.q: Can RIN be used for every paper notarial act?
faqs.a: No. Its statutory definition is limited to acknowledgment of a tangible record.

faqs.q: Does the earlier ink signature eliminate recording?
faqs.a: No. The remote communication still must be audiovisually recorded.

articles.keyword: Correcting a Wyoming certificate with a documented trail
articles.title: Correcting a Wyoming certificate with a documented trail
articles.description: Separate evidence-supported text corrections from changes to a stamp image.
articles.h1: Correcting a Wyoming certificate with a documented trail
articles.lede: The original officer retains control of later changes to a completed Wyoming certificate.

sections.heading: Begin with the transaction evidence
sections.body: A Laramie notary notices that a completed certificate omitted an event detail. The statute permits the performing officer to correct included or omitted information when the change can be evidenced by the transaction journal information where applicable. A recipient's preferred date or desired result is a request to examine, rather than proof that the original event occurred differently.

sections.heading: Date and record the change
sections.body: The correction is dated and initialed by the officer with the corresponding journal notation where applicable. This preserves how the later certificate relates to the recorded act. Correcting an evidentiary omission is different from silently rewriting the underlying transaction. The notary keeps the change within the facts supported by the actual event and its records.

sections.heading: Control delegated edits
sections.body: Only the officer who performed the notarization can make or authorize the correction. If a third party makes the authorized text change, permission is written. Copies of the authorization message and changed certificate are attached to the transaction journal record where applicable. Mere ownership of the document does not authorize the recipient to alter its notarial evidence unilaterally.

sections.heading: Treat the stamp separately
sections.body: The statute does not permit changing or correcting the official impression by hand or by editing its electronic image. An incorrect stamp requires a corrected device. The section permits a subsequent proper impression when the original is missing, illegible or contains wrong information. Apply that particular process together with the required correction documentation.

faqs.q: Can any recipient make a certificate correction?
faqs.a: Only the performing officer can make or authorize it, with the prescribed documentation.

faqs.q: Can a stamp number be repaired by handwriting on its impression?
faqs.a: The statute requires a corrected compliant stamp instead of editing the impression.

articles.keyword: A Wyoming renewed term needs a new official stamp
articles.title: A Wyoming renewed term needs a new official stamp
articles.description: Review both tangible and electronic execution details at renewal.
articles.h1: A Wyoming renewed term needs a new official stamp
articles.lede: An unchanged name does not remove Wyoming's each-renewal stamp replacement requirement.

sections.heading: Use the new commission details
sections.body: A Casper notary renews after six years and plans to keep the former device because the name is unchanged. The statute requires a new stamp upon each renewed commission term. The official certificate supplies the identity and expiration information for the new device. The date printed in the old device is a substantive term detail, rather than decoration that can be ignored.

sections.heading: Order the prescribed design
sections.body: The stamp is a bordered rectangle of approximately one inch by two and one-half inches in blue or black. Its text includes the commissioned name, Notary Public, State of Wyoming, identification number and the expiration wording and date. The State Seal, residence county and other unprescribed content are excluded. A supplier's familiar design still needs to match these actual requirements.

sections.heading: Update electronic execution too
sections.body: An electronic official stamp uses the same prescribed format, color, content and approximate size as the tangible stamp and is copyable with the record. The new-term requirement therefore reaches an old electronic image as well as a physical ink device. A platform storing the former image should not be treated as proof that the image has current commission details.

sections.heading: Disable unusable authority
sections.body: The stamping-device section requires disabling a device when the commission or device date expires, or upon resignation or revocation. The required information is not amended through handwriting or other added text. The notary follows the new-device requirement and security rules instead of writing a current date next to an obsolete official image.

faqs.q: Does renewal replacement apply when the name is unchanged?
faqs.a: Yes. Renewal itself triggers the new-stamp requirement.

faqs.q: Can an old electronic image keep the former expiration?
faqs.a: The electronic stamp must meet the current term and prescribed-content requirements.

articles.keyword: A Wyoming employer's copy differs from the original journal
articles.title: A Wyoming employer's copy differs from the original journal
articles.description: Apply personal control and employment-scope copy retention together.
articles.h1: A Wyoming employer's copy differs from the original journal
articles.lede: Paying for a journal does not remove Wyoming's rules about its use and surrender.

sections.heading: Keep the personal record secure
sections.body: A Cheyenne company buys journal books for its employee-notaries. Each notary still has the statutory responsibility to chronicle all acts and keep the journal and other notarial records securely under sole control. The statute does not let a second notarial officer use the same personal journal merely because the company paid the supply bill.

sections.heading: Plan the employee's departure
sections.body: When employment ends, the notary does not surrender the original journal to the employer without approval from the Secretary of State. That requirement should be addressed before office equipment is returned. A manager's general demand for all purchased items is different from the state approval condition expressly governing the notarial journal.

sections.heading: Provide the permitted copy
sections.body: The statute permits the employer to retain a copy of the journal concerning acts performed within the scope of employment. This provides a particular business-record route while preserving the separate rules for the original. It does not grant the employer unrestricted ownership of unrelated private appointments or permission for another officer to continue notarizing in that journal.

sections.heading: Maintain lawful access and disposition
sections.body: Law-enforcement investigation, court process and state direction have their identified access routes. Surrender or destruction remains limited to the authorities stated in the statute. The education presentation recommends retaining the journal for the term, but that recommendation should not be converted into an automatic destruction authorization at expiration.

faqs.q: Can the employer keep an employment-scope copy?
faqs.a: Yes, as the statute provides.

faqs.q: Does paying for the journal permit taking the original without approval?
faqs.a: No. Original surrender at termination requires the stated state approval.

articles.title: Wyoming provides two directed-signature procedures
articles.description: Use the correct unaffected witnesses and notation for the selected route.
articles.lede: The physically unable principal remains the person directing execution under Wyoming's accommodation provisions.

sections.heading: Determine who will affix the name
sections.body: At a Sheridan appointment, a principal is physically unable to sign a record. The statute permits a directed witness signature or a directed notarial-officer signature with different safeguards. The principal's direction is central to either route. A companion's eagerness to finish should not be confused with the principal choosing and directing the procedure.

sections.heading: Use the one-witness route accurately
sections.body: In the presence of the officer and one witness unaffected by the record, the principal can direct that witness to sign the principal's name. The officer inserts the required statement identifying the signing witness and the principal whose direction was followed under or near the signature. The witness's lack of an interest is one of the actual statutory conditions.

sections.heading: Add the safeguards for officer signing
sections.body: The principal may instead direct the notarial officer to sign in the presence of two witnesses unaffected by the record. The notation identifies the officer, the directing principal and the two witnesses. The number and roles differ from the witness-signing route, so one helpful observer does not satisfy the officer-signing requirements.

sections.heading: Preserve identity and participation
sections.body: The officer identifies every witness through satisfactory evidence and the journal reflects the principal and all participating witnesses. The statute also allows signals or mechanical or electronic means to communicate when oral or written communication is unavailable. Accommodation changes how participation occurs while preserving the required identity, direction and record of the actual event.

faqs.q: How many unaffected witnesses accompany officer signing?
faqs.a: Two under the statutory officer-signing route.

faqs.q: Does accommodation remove witness identity checks?
faqs.a: No. The statute requires satisfactory identification and the stated journal participation record.

articles.keyword: Wyoming official-copy requests have a limited employment exception
articles.title: Wyoming official-copy requests have a limited employment exception
articles.description: Screen source status before making the accurate-copy determination.
articles.h1: Wyoming official-copy requests have a limited employment exception
articles.lede: The statute distinguishes an independent notary from an officer employed by the entity issuing or holding an official record.

sections.heading: Identify the source record
sections.body: A customer asks an independent Wyoming notary to certify a school transcript copied from a government-held original. The prohibited-acts section expressly lists official records issued by public entities, including court records and school transcripts, alongside vital records. A private purpose does not change the public source or make every ordinary notary the record's custodian.

sections.heading: Read the exception precisely
sections.body: The statute provides an exception when the officer is employed by the entity issuing or holding the original version. This is an actual employment condition. A customer saying that an office once emailed the record does not establish that the notary works for the issuing or holding entity. Check the true role before assuming that the exception applies.

sections.heading: Still verify the reproduction
sections.body: A qualifying employment relationship addresses the official-record prohibition but does not establish that the proposed reproduction is full, true and accurate. The copy-certification section requires that determination. An omitted page, changed paragraph or unreadable section still prevents a truthful certification of a complete accurate reproduction even in the eligible employment setting.

sections.heading: Describe the narrow conclusion
sections.body: The certificate identifies the copied record and issuing entity as required, with the proper act evidence and stamp. The accurate-copy finding concerns the reproduction. It does not mean the officer investigated the underlying transaction or guaranteed the truth of every source assertion. Wyoming separately restricts using the notarial role to attest the lawfulness or truthfulness of the underlying record or transaction.

faqs.q: Does Wyoming state an exception for official-copy certification?
faqs.a: Yes, for the specified employment by the issuing or holding entity.

faqs.q: Does that exception waive copy accuracy?
faqs.a: No. The reproduction still must be full, true and accurate.

articles.title: Wyoming refund treatment depends on who cancelled and why
articles.description: Keep compliant fee agreement separate from the later refund question.
articles.h1: Wyoming refund treatment depends on who cancelled and why
articles.lede: Prepaid travel and technology charges do not have one universal outcome under Wyoming's statute and rule.

sections.heading: Agree before incurring the charge
sections.body: A Wyoming mobile notary discusses the travel charge before beginning the trip. The statute ties the rate to the standard IRS mileage rate and requires advance agreement and the separate nonmandated-charge explanation. Technology charges have their own total-fee agreement before the act. A refund provision does not authorize collecting an otherwise unagreed or noncompliant surcharge.

sections.heading: Apply the principal-cancellation facts
sections.body: The travel rule permits retaining a compliant prepaid travel fee when the principal cancels with less than twenty-four hours notice. It also lists the statutory lawful-refusal grounds. These are defined situations. The notary considers what actually happened and does not treat the rule as permission to invent unlimited penalties after every scheduling problem.

sections.heading: Apply the officer-cancellation rule
sections.body: When the officer cancels and does not complete the act, the rule requires refunding the travel fee. That differs from the listed short-notice principal case. A prepaid charge is therefore not automatically retained merely because money arrived before the appointment. The cancellation source and completion facts determine which stated treatment applies.

sections.heading: Keep proofing failure in its category
sections.body: For a compliant prepaid technology fee, the statute permits nonrefund discretion when required KBA or identity proofing fails, whether for fraud or innocent reasons. A failed assessment is not automatically proof of fraud. The officer still reports the real identity outcome and refuses an act that cannot lawfully be completed, independently of the fee decision.

faqs.q: What if the notary cancels without completing the act?
faqs.a: The travel fee must be refunded under the rule.

faqs.q: Must proofing failure be fraudulent for the listed technology-fee discretion?
faqs.a: No. The statute includes innocent failure as well.

articles.keyword: A Wyoming overseas remote principal needs two conditions
articles.title: A Wyoming overseas remote principal needs two conditions
articles.description: Evaluate the foreign prohibition and the record's United States connection together.
articles.h1: A Wyoming overseas remote principal needs two conditions
articles.lede: A U.S. connection does not remove the separate condition concerning the principal's actual foreign location.

sections.heading: Identify the actual locations
sections.body: A Wyoming notarial officer receives a remote request from an individual staying abroad. The record involves U.S. property, but the officer still examines the foreign-location conditions. Customer citizenship or a familiar U.S. mailing address does not replace the fact of where the principal is physically located during the proposed statement or signature.

sections.heading: Check the local prohibition condition
sections.body: The statute requires that the act of making the statement or signing the record not be prohibited in the foreign state where the person is located. This is part of the Wyoming overseas route. A customer saying that remote notarization would be convenient does not resolve that legal condition, and private consent cannot be treated as a general waiver of it.

sections.heading: Identify the listed nexus
sections.body: The record must pertain to a listed U.S. matter, U.S.-jurisdiction property or a substantially U.S.-connected transaction. The condition is about the actual record, rather than the platform's advertising address. Both this nexus and the no-prohibition condition are required. Satisfying one does not automatically satisfy or displace the other.

sections.heading: Continue the particular remote process
sections.body: After the overseas conditions are addressed, use the lawful RON or RIN route, satisfactory identity, same-record steps, sufficient communication, full audiovisual record and appropriate certificate with the actual technology name. The statutory definition of outside the United States also accounts for Puerto Rico, the U.S. Virgin Islands and other U.S. jurisdictions, so it is read before classifying every non-state location as foreign.

faqs.q: Is U.S. property alone enough when local law prohibits the signing?
faqs.a: No. The statute requires both conditions.

faqs.q: Does a U.S. mailing address establish the principal is physically in the United States?
faqs.a: No. The actual location controls that inquiry.

articles.keyword: Advertising a Wyoming notarial service within the authorized role
articles.title: Advertising a Wyoming notarial service within the authorized role
articles.description: Apply disclosure, restricted terminology and official-title limits together.
articles.h1: Advertising a Wyoming notarial service within the authorized role
articles.lede: A required disclosure and the actual services offered are separate parts of compliant notarial advertising.

sections.heading: Describe the permitted role
sections.body: A Wyoming nonattorney prepares a multilingual online advertisement for appointments. The commission does not authorize drafting legal records, legal advice, immigration consultation or representation in the listed proceedings. It also does not authorize compensation for those activities. A service menu should therefore describe what the person is independently authorized to do rather than assume the commission grants a legal practice.

sections.heading: Include the required statement
sections.body: The nonattorney advertisement or representation includes the prescribed or authorized statement prominently in each language used. The statute reaches oral representations and broadcast, print and internet formats. A separate limited size-based fallback applies to the described other formats, where the statement is displayed or provided at the place of performance before the act.

sections.heading: Avoid restricted professional implications
sections.body: The statute restricts notario and notario publico for a person who is not licensed to practice law in Wyoming. The notice does not grant permission to use a separately prohibited term or perform an unauthorized service. Advertising also must not be false or deceptive, so a clear disclosure should correspond to the actual professional role conveyed to the customer.

sections.heading: Keep the official title out of endorsements
sections.body: The official notarial title or stamp cannot be used to endorse, promote, denounce or oppose the listed offerings, including candidates. Adding a nonattorney disclosure does not remove that distinct restriction. The notary examines the proposed use of official office alongside the service-description and warning rules instead of assuming one compliance step resolves every provision.

faqs.q: Does a disclaimer grant immigration-representation authority?
faqs.a: No. The commission and disclaimer do not confer that professional authority.

faqs.q: Does the candidate-use restriction concern only paid advertisements?
faqs.a: The stated official-title and stamp restriction is not limited to paid commercial promotion.

articles.keyword: A Wyoming bordering-state appointment needs recognition checked
articles.title: A Wyoming bordering-state appointment needs recognition checked
articles.description: Separate conditional authority from the actual venue recorded.
articles.h1: A Wyoming bordering-state appointment needs recognition checked
articles.lede: The chapter's bordering-state provision is conditional and does not automatically authorize every neighboring-state appointment.

sections.heading: Identify the physical appointment
sections.body: A Wyoming notary is asked to cross a state border for a signing. The commission authorizes acts within Wyoming and in a bordering state if that state recognizes the officer's authority there. This condition must be checked for the actual jurisdiction. The fact that a state touches Wyoming is the beginning of the inquiry rather than evidence that recognition has been established.

sections.heading: Follow the stated Wyoming requirements
sections.body: When the bordering-state act is allowable, the statute directs the Wyoming notary to adhere to Wyoming laws and rules. The act still needs proper identity, knowing willing execution, certificate, stamp and applicable records. A customer cannot waive those requirements merely because an appointment takes place a few miles beyond the state line.

sections.heading: Use the accurate venue
sections.body: Venue is the state and county where the officer is physically located when performing the act. Keeping a Wyoming home address does not move an out-of-state event back into the home county. The certificate should describe the actual authorized event instead of copying the issuing state's name as though commissioning and physical location were the same fact.

sections.heading: Distinguish recognition of another officer
sections.body: A different section recognizes a lawful act performed by another state's authorized notary in that other state. That recognition gives effect to the act and does not issue a Wyoming commission to that officer. Likewise, an existing Wyoming commission does not by itself prove every neighboring jurisdiction has accepted its use within its own borders.

faqs.q: Does every bordering state automatically qualify?
faqs.a: The actual state's recognition of Wyoming authority must be established.

faqs.q: Does the Wyoming home county always appear as venue?
faqs.a: Venue follows where the officer actually performs the act.
